name: Question 13
problem: Given the curve $r(t)=⟨2{t}^{5}\,,\,{t}^{2}-2⟩,$ $t\in (0,\infty ),$ find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector $⟨1\,,\,-5⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we calculate the derivative of $r(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{5})\,,\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-2)⟩ \\  & =⟨10{t}^{4}\,,\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors  $⟨1\,,\,-5⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular for some value of the parameter $t$ if and only if $⟨1\,,\,-5⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t)=0.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨1\,,\,-5⟩\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ ⟨1\,,\,-5⟩\cdot ⟨10{t}^{4}\,,\,2t⟩ & =0 \\ 1\cdot 10{t}^{4}+(-5)\cdot 2t & =0 \\ 10{t}^{4}-10t & =0 \\ 10t({t}^{3}-1) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\in (0,\infty )$, the only solution is $t=1.$

Finally, since

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨2(1)^{5}\,,\,(1)^{2}-2⟩=⟨2\,,\,-1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

 we conclude that $⟨1\,,\,-5⟩$ and ${r}^{′}(t)$ are perpendicular at the point $(2\,,\,-1).$

Question 13

Given the curve r(t)=⟨2t5,t2−2⟩, t∈(0,∞), find all of the points at which the tangent to the curve is perpendicular to the vector ⟨1,−5⟩.

a
 (64,2)
b
 (64,2) and (116,−74)
c
 (2,−1)
d
 (2,−1) and (116,−74)
e
(116,−74)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we calculate the derivative of r(t): r′(t)=⟨ddt(2t5),ddt(t2−2)⟩=⟨10t4,2t⟩

The vectors ⟨1,−5⟩ and r′(t) are perpendicular for some value of the parameter t if and only if ⟨1,−5⟩⋅r′(t)=0. So, we have

⟨1,−5⟩⋅r′(t)=0⟨1,−5⟩⋅⟨10t4,2t⟩=01⋅10t4+(−5)⋅2t=010t4−10t=010t(t3−1)=0.

Since t∈(0,∞), the only solution is t=1.

Finally, since

r(1)=⟨2(1)5,(1)2−2⟩=⟨2,−1⟩,

we conclude that ⟨1,−5⟩ and r′(t) are perpendicular at the point (2,−1).
